questions.question:
Given below is a cause followed by three effects numbered I, II and III. Read the cause carefully and decide which of the three can be a/the possible effect(s).

Cause - City X has been lashed by lightning and heavy rains for the past two days. The Met Department has predicted more rain in the next 48 hours.

Effect I - The electricity board has decided to increase the tariff by 50 paise per unit in City X.

Effect II - Water-logging is being reported from many areas of City X.

Effect III - Several trees reportedly fell last night on MG Road injuring at least 12 people.

options.text: Both I and II are possible effects.
Only II is a possible effect.
Both II and III are possible effects.
Only I is a possible effect.

questions.solution:
Cause: City X has been lashed by lightning and heavy rains for the past two days, with more rain expected.

**Effect I **This is unrelated to the heavy rains and lightning, as tariff hikes are usually based on financial factors, not weather conditions.

**Effect II** (Water-logging) is a valid effect, as heavy rainfall can easily cause water-logging, especially if drainage systems are overwhelmed, which is a common result of such weather.

**Effect III** (Trees falling) is also possible, as strong winds, heavy rains, and lightning can lead to trees being uprooted, potentially causing injuries and damage.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Both II and III are possible effects."**

questions.question:
In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Which numbers should replace X and Y so that the pattern followed by the two numbers on the left side of :: is the same as that on the right side of ::?

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

X : 529 :: 21 : Y
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is: **√2n**d number - 5 = 1st number

X : 529 → √529 - 5 = 125 → X = 23 - 5 = **18**

Similarly,

21 : Y → √Y - 5 = 21 → √Y = 21 + 5 → Y = 26² = 6**76**

Hence, the correct answer is "X = 18, Y = 676".

questions.question:
In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Which numbers should replace X and Y so that the pattern followed by the two numbers on the left side of :: is same as that on the right side of ::?

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

X : 243 :: 17 : Y
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is: 1st number **× 9 + 18** = 2nd number.

X : 243 → X × 9 + 18 = 243 → X × 9 = 225 → X = 225 / 9 = **25**

Similarly, 

17 : Y → 17 × 9 + 18 = 153 + 18 = **171**

Hence, the correct answer is "**X = 25, Y = 171**".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statements.

Statements:

All doors are gates.

No door is a lock.

Conclusion:

(I) Some locks are gates.

(II) No lock is a door.
questions.solution:
**Statements:**

All doors are gates.

No door is a lock.

The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d62ce72469dc962fb9be7f366485043c0b6645141758d4aada51a7766339b9f.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09166d53c6fb6ebf4c9c7f4b35e66650928d349a9a53fa5b12cce0d841c5a861.png] 

**Conclusion:**

(I) Some locks are gates.- **False **(because because there is no direct relation given between lock and gates, so it can be possible but not definite)

(II) No lock is a door. - **True **(because No door is a lock given. So, No lock is a door too)

Hence, the correct answer is "Only conclusion (II) follows".
